title.en: Revolutionaries, Left movements and the road to Quit India

text.en: After Gandhi suspended non-cooperation, many young Indians lost patience and picked up arms, while others read about the Russian Revolution. Together they pushed the freedom struggle in new directions.

The Communist Party of India was founded at Tashkent in October 1920 by M.N. Roy and others, and the Kanpur Conspiracy Case of 1924 tried leaders like Singaravelar.
In 1924 the Hindustan Republican Army was formed to overthrow colonial rule by armed rebellion, and in 1925 its members looted a government train at Kakori.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and others renamed it the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in 1928.
Sanders, the police officer linked to the lathi charge that killed Lajpat Rai, was assassinated, and Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a smoke bomb in the Assembly in 1929.
Surya Sen's Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930 declared a provisional revolutionary government.
In 1934 Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev and Minoo Masani formed the Congress Socialist Party.
The Government of India Act 1935 offered provincial autonomy with all subjects transferred to Indian ministers, though only about ten percent could vote.
In the 1937 elections the Congress won seven of eleven provinces and formed ministries in eight, including Madras.
Ministers took a salary of Rs. 500 instead of Rs. 2,000 and repealed repressive acts, and temple entry laws were passed.
In 1939 the Congress ministries resigned because the government joined the war without consulting them.
In 1940 the August Offer led Gandhi to start individual satyagraha, and Vinoba Bhave offered it first on 17 October 1940.
The Cripps Mission of March 1942 offered Dominion status after the war but failed, and Gandhi called it a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.
On 8 August 1942 the All India Congress Committee at Bombay passed the Quit India Resolution and Gandhi gave the call to Do or Die.

problem.en: How did revolutionary and left movements differ from Gandhian methods?

text.en: Revolutionaries like the HSRA used violence against officials to shake the government.

why.en: Bhagat Singh and Surya Sen are examples.

text.en: Left groups like the CPI and the Congress Socialist Party stressed workers and peasants.
Gandhi relied on mass non-violent action.
